title: Highlands Ranch
name: Highlands Ranch
metaTitle: Highlands Ranch 1031 Exchange Services | 1031 Exchange Denver
metaDescription: Highlands Ranch 1031 exchange guidance for medical office, Town Center retail, and HOA-governed commercial property in unincorporated Douglas County.

sections.html: Highlands Ranch is a master-planned community in unincorporated Douglas County, south of Denver off C-470. There's no city hall here, an HOA runs a lot of what a city government would normally handle, and that governance quirk actually matters for anyone underwriting commercial property in this submarket.

sections.heading: No City Hall Changes How Things Get Approved
sections.html:
Since Highlands Ranch is unincorporated, land use and zoning approvals run through Douglas County rather than a city planning department, and the Highlands Ranch Community Association layers its own design and use review on top of that for anything inside the master plan boundaries. A buyer used to dealing with a single city planning office needs to budget for two separate approval processes here, not one.

Highlands Ranch Backcountry Wilderness Area sits along the community's southern edge, a large tract of preserved open space that the original master plan set aside permanently. That preservation caps how far commercial development can push south, which is part of why the retail and medical office inventory here has stayed concentrated along a handful of established corridors rather than spreading out.

sections.heading: The Property Types That Actually Show Up
sections.html:
Commercial inventory in Highlands Ranch runs toward:

  • medical and dental office buildings serving the residential population
  • retail centers with a grocery or big-box tenant carrying the center
  • Highlands Ranch Town Center lifestyle retail and restaurant space
  • small professional office buildings near the University Boulevard corridor

sections.heading: This Is a Rooftop-Driven Market
sections.html:
Almost everything commercial in Highlands Ranch exists to serve the residential population living around it, not regional traffic passing through. That means retail and medical tenants here lease against household counts and drive times, not highway visibility, and a buyer should underwrite rents against local demographic trends rather than comparing them to a highway-fronting Aurora or Lakewood parcel. A lender familiar with rooftop-driven retail underwriting will move faster on this kind of deal than one that only handles highway-frontage retail models tied to drive-by traffic counts.

Industrial and distribution space is essentially absent inside Highlands Ranch itself. Anyone looking for that asset class needs to look toward Centennial or the E-470 corridor instead, since the master plan here was laid out for residential and rooftop-serving retail from the start.

sections.heading: Diligence Specific to This Community
sections.html:
Pull both the Douglas County zoning file and the Highlands Ranch Community Association's design review file before assuming a use is approved. Confirm any HOA assessment or covenant obligations that run with a commercial parcel, since those can carry real annual cost that doesn't show up on a standard title report the way a city special assessment district would.

University Boulevard runs the length of Highlands Ranch and connects north toward Denver and south toward the Lone Tree and Park Meadows area, and most of the community's medical and professional office inventory sits along that corridor. A buyer comparing two Highlands Ranch office buildings should check their exact position on University Boulevard, since access and visibility shift noticeably between the northern and southern stretches.

sections.heading: Positioning a Highlands Ranch Identification
sections.html: A medical office or Town Center retail asset here pairs well with a Littleton or Centennial property on an identification list, giving an investor rooftop-driven retail alongside a more traditional office or industrial asset elsewhere in the south Denver metro. A qualified intermediary coordinating this exchange should confirm the HOA's transfer and estoppel process early, since it can add a step to closing that a standard commercial closing wouldn't have. That estoppel letter should spell out any outstanding assessments or pending covenant enforcement actions tied to the parcel, since those obligations transfer to the new owner at closing rather than staying with the seller. Form 8824 preparation on a Highlands Ranch exchange should note any HOA-related expense separately from standard operating costs, since a tax advisor will want that distinction clear on the return. A replacement property identification for Highlands Ranch should note the exact corridor or center by name in the paperwork, rather than only the community, since retail and medical office rents vary meaningfully between the northern and southern stretches of University Boulevard. A rent roll comparison between a Town Center parcel and a University Boulevard medical building should never be blended into a single community-wide average, since each responds to a different tenant base and a different set of demand drivers.

faqs.q: Why does Highlands Ranch have an HOA instead of a city government?
faqs.a: It's unincorporated Douglas County land, so county government handles zoning while the Highlands Ranch Community Association layers its own design and use review on top for anything inside the master plan.

faqs.q: Is industrial property available in Highlands Ranch?
faqs.a: Essentially no. The master plan was laid out for residential and rooftop-serving retail, so investors looking for industrial or distribution space should look toward Centennial or the E-470 corridor instead.

faqs.q: What drives retail demand in this submarket?
faqs.a: Household counts and drive times from the surrounding residential population, not highway visibility. Underwrite rents against local demographics rather than comparing to a highway-fronting parcel elsewhere in the metro.

faqs.q: Does the HOA add cost to owning commercial property here?
faqs.a: It can. Confirm any assessment or covenant obligations tied to a specific parcel, since those carry real annual cost that a standard title report may not fully capture.

faqs.q: What pairs well with a Highlands Ranch identification?
faqs.a: A Littleton or Centennial property, giving the exchange rooftop-driven retail alongside a more traditional office or industrial asset in the south Denver metro.
